title: Drone Strikes Hit Kyiv and Other Ukrainian Cities
summary: Imagine a building where scientists work, right in the middle of a big city. On Monday, a drone hit the National Academy of Sciences in Kyiv, Ukraine's capital. Ukraine's President, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, said nine people were killed and more than 80 were hurt across the country that day. Kyiv's mayor, Vitali Klitschko, said 24 people were injured in the capital, and six of them were in the hospital. Other cities were hit too. In Zaporizhzhia, 32 people were hurt. In Synelnykove, one person was killed at a logistics office. Zelenskyy said Ukraine is having a hard time stopping Russia's new jet-powered drones. They fly faster and higher than older propeller drones. Out of 120 drones fired at Ukraine, 90 were jet-powered, and Ukraine shot down 57 per cent of them. He said new interceptors are being tested. Ukraine's foreign minister asked allies for more air defences. Russia's President, Vladimir Putin, says Russia is not ordering a new call-up of soldiers. He called that idea "utter nonsense."
why_it_matters: When countries fight, ordinary people lose their homes, their schools and sometimes their lives, which is why kids around the world pay attention to news like this.

background_read: Kyiv is the capital of Ukraine (a country in eastern Europe), and Russia is the much bigger country next to it.
Russia launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, and drones have become one of the most common weapons in that war.

Volodymyr Zelenskyy (Ukraine's president since 2019) and Vladimir Putin (Russia's president) lead the two countries, while Ukraine's allies, such as the United States and countries in Europe, send it weapons and air-defence systems.
Article_Structure: WHO: Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, Kyiv's mayor Vitali Klitschko, and Russia's President Vladimir Putin.
WHAT: Drone strikes hit Kyiv and other Ukrainian cities, killing nine people and injuring more than 80 across the country.
WHERE: Cities in Ukraine, including Kyiv, Zaporizhzhia and Synelnykove.
WHY: Russia's new jet-powered drones fly faster and higher than older propeller drones, so Ukraine is struggling to shoot them down and is asking allies for more air defences.

perspectives.description: Ukrainian leaders say they need more air defences and are testing new interceptors to catch the faster jet-powered drones.
President Putin says Russia is not ordering a new call-up of soldiers and called that idea 'utter nonsense.'
Nine people were killed and more than 80 were hurt in a single day, including a strike on a science building in the middle of Ukraine's capital.
